scene: Inferno XIII — Pier della Vigna, wounded branch and speaking wood
source: Dante Inferno XIII verses 1–108; Princeton Dante Project and University of Leeds Canto XIII summaries
story: After Nessus departs, Dante and Virgil enter a pathless wood with dark leaves, twisted boughs, thorns and nesting Harpies.
Dante hears lamentations without seeing human speakers and initially cannot identify their source.
Virgil tells Dante to break a twig to establish what produces the voices; Dante breaks a small branch from a thornbush.
The wounded wood bleeds dark blood and protests aloud. Dante drops the twig in alarm.
Virgil apologizes, saying Dante would not otherwise have believed that the voices come from these transformed souls.
The speaker recounts his service to Emperor Frederick II and loss of favor, revealing his identity as Pier della Vigna.
Pier explains the souls' transformation into trees and the Harpies' wounding of them; their fate at the final judgment remains part of the testimony.
The later pursuit of spendthrifts and the unnamed Florentine belongs to the next stage.

semanticSomatic.semantic: Confusion between unseen source and visible object; contact produces evidence but inflicts harm

somatic.gesture: hears lament, snaps a twig as directed, then drops it
somatic.result: branch is wounded; blood and protest become evident

semanticSomatic.semantic: A person remains capable of testimony in an externally unfamiliar, confined form

somatic.gesture: wounded trunk emits dark blood and audible complaint
somatic.result: previously mislocated voice becomes identifiable as the tree itself

semanticSomatic.semantic: Correct a false assumption and acknowledge the cost of obtaining evidence

somatic.gesture: asks Dante to test the twig then apologizes to the wounded speaker
somatic.result: the observer gains understanding but the inflicted injury is not erased

semanticSomatic.semantic: Ongoing disturbance of the bound inhabitants

somatic.gesture: settle among the thorn trees and tear their foliage
somatic.result: the suffering of the tree-spirits continues

cipher.operator: HEAR -> MISLOCATE -> BREAK -> BLEED+SPEAK -> RECOGNIZE -> APOLOGIZE
cipher.notation: VOICE? -> (1) BREAK(TWIG) -> TREE{BLEED || SPEAK} -> PIER_IDENTITY -> [2] APOLOGIZE
cipher.keyInvariant: A familiar exterior does not determine whether an entity is capable of speech or experiencing harm. Recognition does not undo the inflicted damage.
cipher.costOfObservation: The test changes and wounds its subject; this is not passive or non-destructive observation.
cipher.roleClarification: Pier is already a speaking person in the poem's supernatural world; this is a literary transformation, not an actual plant becoming a human through chemistry.
